summary: Configured node1 as the source of truth for `/etc/inventory/app.conf` and node2 as its synchronized target. A secure atomic push runs every minute, well within the 15-minute requirement. Both nodes were restarted sequentially and recovered successfully. The source was initially absent, so it was initialized as an empty root-owned 0644 file without fabricating application settings.
actions_performed: Generated a dedicated synchronization key on node1.
Installed an address-restricted, forced-command receiver on node2.
Created and enabled a one-minute systemd synchronization timer on node1.
Proved an automatic test change reached node2 in approximately 44 seconds, then removed the test marker.
Verified final source and target hashes match.
Restarted node1 and node2 one at a time and verified changed boot IDs, service recovery, data persistence, and post-restart synchronization.

evidence.requirement: Synchronize changes from node1 to node2 within 15 minutes
evidence.summary: The timer was scheduled at one-minute intervals. A source change at 20:11:55 appeared on node2 with the same SHA-256 by 20:12:39.

evidence.requirement: Final synchronization service and data health
evidence.summary: The timer is active and enabled with a one-minute interval; its last service result succeeded. Both files are root-owned 0644 and have identical SHA-256 hashes.

Healthy baseline boot ID d052eb57… was captured, restart was acknowledged, and the new boot ID 3961bb89… was observed. The timer recovered active/enabled and completed a successful post-restart transfer accepted by node2.

Healthy baseline boot ID ebf808c5… was captured, restart was acknowledged, and the new boot ID a0af2562… was observed. SSH, receiver credentials, target data, and post-restart synchronization all recovered.
